title: Great tool for those with ADHD
body:
The Today Habit Tracker app has been monumental for me as someone with severe ADHD. Being able to plan ahead and create daily and weekly routines, along with corresponding widgets, has made scheduling and planning daily life a breeze. The app is simple, elegant, and full of features. I have subscribed to a year of premium due to its benefits. However, I’ve noticed it lacks some critical functionality and contains a couple bugs. I’d love to see an update with some or all of the following addressed!
* When selecting “view/edit data” on a custom chart, the app crashes — there is no way to change, remove, or edit the number entered originally.
* Some health categories I am interested in displaying are missing — like medications taken/skipped
* Being able to launch shortcuts or apps within a habit could be a great feature to make completing tasks simpler. * I would love to be able to create a section for “bad habits” — most of what I use the app for is daily and weekly tasks like laundry, meds, and exercise. Having a section for bad habits, like arguing, vaping, drinking, etc. where I could keep track of these habits and focus on quitting them could be great.
* I would also love to see more integration with other third party apps, like Spotify (for quick launching playlists and choosing tunes for each habit), Calm/Headspace (for quickly starting a random or preselected meditation), Nike Run Club (for starting workouts quickly and seeing more detailed information), and possibly smart home apps — like HomeKit, Alexa, LG Thinq, or Tuya — setting routines from within the app and having access to information like washer/dryer time remaining would be monumental.
* The Pillow sleep tracking app, which is made by the same developer, isn’t integrated at all into this app — with sleeping habits being integral to a healthy lifestyle, I’d love to see more feature tie ins between the two.
* Milestones, which are essentially mini checklist widgets sitting below a habit, don’t automatically reset daily with no option to have the app do so. I use this feature for tasks such as my meditation routine, morning rituals, and logging medication I have taken on a specific day. Being able to choose to have these lists reset daily, as well as being able to see a history of what was checked off on what day and when, would go a long way for me.
* The Welzen meditation app, which is prominently featured on a widget, isn’t available in the U.S. app store — once the widget is added, it is functionally useless. I’d love to see a revamped mindfulness feature!
Overall, this app is a great tool for those who need it, and with some improvement, would be an instant purchase for me! As these bugs and missing features are addressed, I will definitely up my rating to 5 stars — this app is very close to being perfect!

title: What Habit Will You Start Today?
body:
If you want to create a new habit, there is no shortage of apps on the App Store to help you reach your goal. Today eschews the typical list-of-habits interface and instead shows each goal or habit on its own screen, complete with gorgeous background. Swipe left and right between goals, double-tap to check in.

Also atypical in an app of this type is the ability to add additional data. Swipe up to review cards of different types that you have attached to the goal: charts, counters, photos, milestones, notes — anything that might help propel you toward your desired outcome. You can even include Apple Health metrics. (It would be nice, though, if adding weight data in another app would immediately register a check-in.)

Today supports multiple reminders per habit (an important feature for me) and its notifications are rich and actionable. It's Today screen widget makes it easy to update your progress without getting into the app. And I like that you can set daily, weekly, or monthly goals; that specific days can be set for daily goals; and that daily habits can have multiple completions per day.

Another neat feature (if you're into that kind of thing) is that Today awards badges for total completions and streaks. And tucked away in a dark corner are stats for things like habit persistence and what day is the best for getting things done. My only disappointment with the app is its inability to properly track bad habits. If I were tracking (as I am now) whether or not I've had *any* soda, a single check-in could indicate success in abstaining for the day. But if I only want to *limit* my intake to, say, two sodas a day, I can't both log each drink and show success for not going over the limit. Still, the app is fairly new and appears to be supported, and it's well worth the small price for the premium features. I am looking forward to seeing what new features and cards the developer dreams up and maybe this shortcoming will be addressed.

title: Great potential, not quite there though.
body:
I have been through every app in the app store for habit trackers - this one is my favorite because it doesn’t feel like just another to do list, calendar, or chore. It’s actually fun! It’s personal, and it’s genuinely helpful. I love it. A couple problems I run into though are:
1. I lost all my data after the app crashed when I was deleting my old cover photos. That was a real bummer and since then I’ve noticed the app doesn’t automatically back up your data like it says it does. 
2. The milestone card is not useful as is. I wish you could have recurring milestones.. and you might say whatever needs to be tracked on a  recurring basis could be done with the other cards... but the milestone card is cool because it allows you to type out words so that you can add even more personalization to your habit instead of just tracking tally marks, which I think really adds an important component to motivation. 
3. The chart card is wonderful but it really needs to show CUMULATIVE data RELATIVE to your goal, not averages. I wish the Goal could be reset as well. 
4. The counter card is really great... no complaints about that.
5. I think the meditation card is cool, but I’m a subscriber to Headspace, so it would be nice I could have that data imported. 
6. The journal card is perfect. The photo card is perfect. 
7. The interface is perfect. 

As a side note I really love that you can add as many cards as possible. 

I’ve emailed the developers about these quirks so I know they are working on some of these things already. I don’t mean to be repetitive it’s just that I literally love this app so much and I’ve been telling all my friends about it... it’s so close to perfect that it makes me kind of impatient for the next update! Thanks for creating this app!!

title: App helped me drop 60lbs at the Gym!!
body:
I’ve always struggled to build a consistent habit of working out. Last year I downloaded Today in the hopes of finding a solution that will help me visualize my goals. This has been one of the best downloads I’ve ever made. I even paid for premium pack! 

1) Easy to use interface makes it super simple to check-in your habit. If you use the widget — makes it even easier! 

2) Streak Calendar allows me to see how many days of the week I’ve been consistent. It marks the day in a green box to give you a sense of accomplishment! 

3) You can add different cards to your habit tracker. For example, there is a journal entry card I use to log which body part I’ve worked on and how much time I’ve spent in Cardio. I also use the photo card to take my progress pics! 

4) It backs up to iCloud Drive so you don’t lose your tracking data, streaks, badges, and settings. 

5) Super customizable so your goals can be changed to daily, weekly, monthly, even asking which days of the week or how many days of the week you want to check-in your habit. Also, it sends you reminders if you allow notifications. 

6) You can log multiple habits. For example, I use it to log my gym workouts, I use it to practice mindfulness, and have used it to build a habit of reading more. 

There is so much more this app offers that I can’t possibly cover in a review, but it’s definitely worth the free download and, personally, it’s worth the premium pack price too. This app helped me build a consistent habit of going to the gym 4-5 times a week and I’ve dropped 60lbs since using it!

title: ...and Apple won’t give me a refund
body:
It’s been two days with the premium version and I already hate it. 

In my attempt to stick to my routine and build goals, I must have searched for 2 hours different apps that were not only easy to use, aesthetically pretty but also showed me my progress over the long term and, most importantly, let me have multiple reminders though-out the day. Believe it or not, there are very few apps that let you have multiple check-ins. This app (I thought) fit all the criteria.

After downloading, what I thought was the starter (free) version, I soon realized I accidentally bought the premium (oops) but decided to try it out. After putting all my routines and goals in, complete with reminders. I waited for the first bell to remind me. Nothing. Thinking, maybe I forget to check and save my reminder option, I went back - nope, everything checked and save. I waited for the next reminder. Nothing. I deleted everything and started over, making sure everything was checked and saved. Still nothing. 

As a someone who needs an extra push sometimes, even in the form of a bell or simple pop-up message on my phone, this app is useless. All pretty pictures and no value. 

However, this experience did cement three things in me (things that, for whatever reason, I didn’t listen to earlier) and teach me another: 
 1. Apple (post Steve Jobs) has terrible customer service. They make you wait two days just to tell you no. Steve Jobs would have given me a refund. 
2. If you need reminders, don’t bother with apps, just use the pre-set alarm function in your phone (on iPhone, it’s under Clock) or watch. You’ve already bought it & it’s more dependable. 
3. If you want to keep track of routines & habits, don’t rely on an app to do your work for you. Either set up an Excel spreadsheet that lists the date, time, & activity. You can then sort and chart your progress easily after a set period of time. P.S. you can also set alarms in Excel. Don’t like Excel, Google “Bullet Journal” on how to keep a routine & habit tracker. 
4. Pay attention to what you are doing, you’ll never get that time back.

body:
There is a lot to love about this app but it is missing a few key functions that make habit tracking more successful. In addition to “check ins” (positive score) there ought to be a way to record “missed check -ins” (negative score) and just also a way to log days where you missed your habit but it was intentional (neutral/no penalty score). The metrics of only seeing your number of check ins is a useless metric without also seeing those days you dropped the ball. 

It’s also be great to see two habits side by side so you can see if your “early to bed” habit has a correlation to “deep work” the following day—another reason why showing “missed” days would be useful. 

I like how you can schedule a habit that has a once/week (or whatever) frequency but I’d love to see a countdown on that habit so you know, “3 more days left in week to accomplish habit”

The ability to add in widgets is amazing! Design is beautiful ... Just wish some of the basic habit-tracking functionality was more useful.

title: Light years ahead of other habit trackers--get Premium!
body:
This is the most beautiful app currently on my phone. The functionality matches the looks. The ability to add counters, totals, milestones and other metrics to a habit makes this the most powerful habit app out there. You can see the data behind your habits. I love that I can add covers to the habits, I've added related artwork that subtly reminds me why I'm doing the habit in the first place. 

One reviewer said that since each habit has it's own page, it makes marking off many habits difficult. That makes no sense to me. The main page has a complete list of all Habits and you can mark off basic habit completions off from there as you would in other habit apps. The beauty behind this app is you can really dive deep into your specific habit and keep track of important progress/data. 

For example, I have a sales goal to contact 50 prospects per day. I can use a resettable counter to count each time I make a contact. I can use the custom chart to track my daily total. And I can use another counter to keep track of my totals for the year. And I can use milestones to keep track of long-term goals (e.g. 1000 contacts). 

The only thing I'd add would be the ability to export everything to CSV so I can also look at the data on Google Sheets. Also a Slack integration and desktop app would get me really excited... :)

title: Great app, great pricing model
body:
First and foremost this is a great app for allowing you to hold yourself accountable and create new habits or squash old ones. It does exactly what it says it does and does so in a very easy to use and overall "pretty" interface. 

I love that I suggested a feature I would like to see and received a timely, personal response from the development team. 

Lastly, I love the, what I'm calling, "payment model" this company is using. The app is free to download with an available in-app purchase. The free app allows you to add a habit and try it out fully for that one habit. Then if you like it, pay $4.99 (well worth it) to unlock unlimited habits as well as other niceties like Touch ID support to lock the app down and backup via the cloud. I know this model doesn't work for every developer or app but it certainly is perfection here. 

Highly recommend this if you want a simple way to keep track of habits and are trying to make positive change in your life.

title: It's an investment. No matter the price.

We all picture ourselves as if we had achieved whatever we set our minds too. As if we had become the person we aspire to be. The stepping stones, the incremental building blocks to this imaginative picture, they are our goals. 

To maintain these stepping stones to success you need simplicity, the ease of simply knowing you did the right thing and you've come ever further on your journey. But you also want to option for complexity. The knowledge of how you've gotten there. Of how far you've come.

This app gives you that option. The cost may seem high but the reward is ever higher. Other apps charge you for instant gratification. For amusement. This app provides you with the tools to become a better, happier, more successful person.

It cost nothing. You won't regret it if you're truly determined.

title: A happy lifestyle is worth $5
body:
I understand that people are upset about the limited functionality and forced paid version for $5. On one hand, I agree that it should have been a paid app from the start, or at least allow 2-3 habits. 

But who cares. $5, in the grand scheme of things, is nothing. That's one cup of coffee. And to anyone using an Apple product to download the app, they already forked out $600+ for the hardware,  which is substantial. The stigma here is that the App Store is so utterly saturated with free/freemium apps that I think a lot of times we forget the amount of work that goes into development... And that its intended to provide developers with an income. 

The app can be improved, and I'm sure that it will. But the $5 investment is worth every penny and more if the app gets you to do what it's intended to. The return on investment in sheer productivity or your quality of life is phenomenal if you consider that this app can help you make, and keep, good habits. And if even ONE of my current habits sticks (Floss, Meditate, Read, Run, Bodyweight Exercise), the effect it will have on my life will be much more than $5.

•a coupon for discounted goodies, like Starbucks maybe.
•small amounts of "coins" or other game currency in fun iOS games (maybe you could partner with someone)

My one complaint though. Why aren't there notification widgets for it? I use my today screen every day and it's nuts that I can't add my daily habits to the daily overview. That's why there are only 4 stars.

Otherwise, it's great (so far)
